[00:00] Samir: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, happy new year. Quick roll call, we wanted to use this slot to lock the renewal amendment and the multi-region plan before procurement kicks off. Um, quick agenda: capacity numbers, EU/APAC activation path, security blockers, and next steps. Mira, want to kick us off with current production posture?
[00:18] Dr. Mira: Yeah thanks Samir. So uh in production we're at about 70 million inference tokens a day, burst to 95M at peak. Latency SLO for our customer-facing triage app is "p90 < 220ms" today, that's been tight, um largely on hosted but we've had some transient throttles during high-volume mornings. We're also starting pilot for PHI routing which is why we're looking again at private VPC options.
[00:45] Tom: Just to add, our infra is k8s with a private VPC on GCP, we've got a sidecar pattern for model calls and we're managing KV cache in Redis. We really prefer minimal changes to app code.
[01:08] Lena: Sounds good. From Redwood's side, hi I'm Lena, SE. We ran the initial telemetry and the token distribution shows 60% short responses <120 tokens and 20% long tails. That maps to your latency pressure in the mornings. For the uplift, we modeled a 30% committed capacity increase as a conservative starter which should cover expected growth through Q2.
[01:30] Dr. Mira: 30% seems reasonable. What's the rough hardware footprint for that?
[01:36] Samir: Good question — for Dedicated we'd propose adding a pool equivalent to 4x A100-80GB GPUs (we call it a medium pool) which gives you headroom and allows isolation for PHI flows. If you want to avoid full Dedicated for PHI, we can also do private VPC hosted nodes — basically Private control plane with customer VPC peering.
[01:58] Janelle: Quick security flag — any private option needs to support our KMS (HashiCorp Vault in our case) and audit log retention for 2 years. Also need to know about data at rest encryption and where keys live.
[02:12] Noah: Yep, we'll make sure we include KMS notes. Redwood's Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM — we have integrations with Google CMEK and HashiCorp Vault in our private deployments, but we will confirm the exact flow for cross-region replication.
[02:30] Tom: Is there an expected maintenance window for Dedicated pool scale-ups? We can't have disruptions to the morning triage cadence.
[02:38] Lena: The runtime supports rolling capacity additions with traffic draining; typical window for adding a medium pool is 20-30 minutes for activation, no downtime expected. We'll do canary traffic routing and automatic fallback to hosted model variants if there are issues.
[02:58] Dr. Mira: Okay, good. Can we get an SLA figure for rolling upgrades?
[03:04] Samir: For Dedicated customers we provide an SLA for availability of serving endpoints — we'll attach the SLA text in the amendment. For rolling upgrades, we generally meet our availability target > 99.9% with configured failovers.
[03:20] Omar: Curious on pricing — how much would that 30% bump cost and what are the options for committed tiers vs burst?
[03:28] Samir: We've prepared three scenarios: conservative (30% uplift), aggressive (60% uplift), and staged (30% now + 30% reserved burst). I'll share a worksheet after the call with per-token estimates and fixed pool fees. Roughly speaking the committed pool delta is about $23k/month for the medium pool — but I'll send exact line items.
[03:52] Janelle: For compliance we'll need SOC2 artifact, encryption writeups, and an architectural diagram showing where PHI sits and what stays inside the VPC.
[04:01] Lena: We'll attach the SOC2 summary and architecture whiteboard. One note: for PHI you might prefer Private (VPC) with dedicated pools as that gives you full network isolation and customer-managed KMS. Hosted can be configured with stronger contractual controls, but there is still shared control plane.
[04:22] Dr. Mira: For EU region activation — timeline? We need EU for data residency for a subset of customers.
[04:28] Samir: We can enable EU region in two phases: 1) Hosted EU region activation — that's fastest, 3-5 business days for routing and model variants; 2) Private EU pilot — that's 3-4 weeks for VPC peering, KMS integration and audit configuration. Both can be overlapped; recommended approach is spin up hosted EU first for immediate residency and then migrate PHI flows to Private EU pilot.
[04:50] Tom: APAC — we want it on-demand for campaign bursts during APAC trading hours. Do you support burst-only regions?
[04:58] Lena: Yes, we support regional burst routing. You can configure APAC as a burst region with a reserved burst capacity and our smart routing will failover to US/EU if APAC is saturated. That keeps baseline cost down.
[05:12] Janelle: About audit logs — can we get sub-second request logs? We need request IDs and user de-id fields for some investigations.
[05:20] Noah: We capture per-request tracing with IDs and offer configurable retention. For Private deployments we can stream logs to your Cloud Logging project or to a S3/GCS bucket. There may be egress considerations — we'll detail those.
[05:34] Dr. Mira: Are there any performance regressions expected if we enable quantization for cost saving? We've seen weird token jitter in other runs.
[05:41] Lena: Quantized variants can reduce GPU memory and cost significantly; for most models we validate output quality with a prompt-suite. There can be small latency differences, usually better, but output drift is model-dependent. Part of the benchmark we'll run includes a quality regression check against your smoke prompt set.
[05:59] Tom: OK, to make this concrete: we want a pilot that meets these points — (a) Dedicated medium pool for PHI flows in EU (Private), (b) Hosted EU region for non-PHI traffic within 5 business days, (c) APAC burst configuration for campaigns, (d) pricing worksheet with committed tiers and burst pricing, (e) security package with KMS flow and SOC2 artifacts. Is that a fair list?
[06:22] Samir: Yes that's exactly what we'll deliver. I'll walk through next steps and owners.
[06:28] Samir: Action owners inline: Samir -> pricing worksheet, contract amendment draft; Lena -> benchmark infra + run; Noah -> security artifacts & log config notes; Janelle (Elara) -> provide compliance requirements and KMS contact; Tom -> infra access for benchmark (temporary service account).
[06:45] Janelle: One more thing — procurement insisted on a 12-month term with an option to scale monthly. Is Redwood flexible on a rolling capacity amendment?
[06:53] Samir: We support 12-month base with monthly scaling addenda; we can draft a clause for tiered commits and optional top-ups.
[07:02] Dr. Mira: Great. On the benchmark — what metrics will you collect? We want latency p50/p90/p99, token throughput, GPU utilization, tail latencies for long prompts, and quality regressions.
[07:13] Lena: We'll collect all of those. Specifically: p50/p90/p99, tokens/sec aggregate, average GPU utilization per device, KV cache hit rates, and evaluation scores on your smoke prompts. We'll provide a spreadsheet with baseline vs candidate.
[07:29] Tom: How invasive is the benchmarking? We don't want changes to our runtime.
[07:33] Lena: Minimal. We'll request a service account, a small test namespace, and a traffic replay (we can accept a redacted replay). We can also run a shaded traffic test with synthetic load if the replay isn't possible.
[07:48] Omar: Anything we should escalate to legal/security internally?
[07:51] Janelle: I'll escalate KMS vendor confirmation and retention SLA. Also want to review the data processing addendum early.
[07:58] Samir: We'll send a DPA template with the amendment.
[08:02] [brief cross-talk and screen-share noise]
[08:20] Lena: Timeline recap: pricing + amendment by Jan 7; security artifacts by Jan 10; benchmark kick-off week of Jan 11; 2-week benchmark run Jan 11-25; procurement review/interal signoff last week of Jan. That would aim to have amended contract signed by mid-February.
[08:40] Dr. Mira: That timeline fits our internal Q2 planning. For the benchmark, can we add an evaluation of autoregressive vs chat-style conversation models? We run both.
[08:50] Lena: Sure — include both model families. We'll bring model-variant perf numbers and expected quantization impacts.
[08:57] Tom: Any billing proration for mid-term scale-ups?
[09:00] Samir: We prorate new pool charges for partial months; for reserved commits we pro-rate the fixed pool fee. Burst usage is billed per token with thresholds as in the worksheet.
[09:12] Dr. Mira: Okay, can we also do a short technical deep dive after the benchmark to verify failover behavior?
[09:18] Noah: Absolutely — we can schedule a 45-minute SE deep dive to walk through tracing and fallbacks.
[09:24] Janelle: From a security POV, I'd like a short runbook for incident response for model drift or data leakage scenarios.
[09:31] Lena: We'll prepare a short runbook and the logging artifact mapping.
[09:36] Omar: One question on competitors — we evaluated Anthropic and an in-house path; cost was a big driver. Do you have benchmarks comparing costs for similar throughput?
[09:45] Samir: We have an internal benchmarking deck; we'll share a cost-per-token and latency comparison for common model families. Note: comparisons are approximate depending on model choices and quantization.
[09:56] Dr. Mira: Alright, if there's nothing else let's recap owners and close.
[10:01] Samir: Owners recap: Samir (pricing + amendment) due Jan 7; Lena (benchmark infra + run) kickoff Jan 11, results Jan 25; Noah (security pack) due Jan 10; Janelle (requirements) due Jan 10; Tom (service account) before kickoff. We'll send calendar invites for benchmark kickoff and the SE deep dive.
[10:18] Dr. Mira: Thanks all. That covers it.
